title: Repair queue

steps.prompt:
Record w1: title "Replace pump", state open, priority high, hours 3.5.
Record w2: title "Inspect valve", state accepted, priority normal, hours 0.
Record w3: title "Calibrate gauge", state closed, priority low, hours 2.25.
Show all source fields in a table.

Evolve this existing prototype, not a new application. Set the English title of the existing table to "Repair queue" and the English caption of its title field to "Request". Show the existing columns in this order: state, priority, title, hours. Keep the stored record identities and values, and all other existing behavior unchanged.

Extend the existing Repair queue table. Add text search over title only, not over state, priority or hours. Also add a separate equality filter on priority with choices high, normal and low. Both controls must compose: searching pump while filtering low returns no records; clearing both restores the three records. Keep all existing records, field captions and column order unchanged.

Add a local record command labeled "Accept" for the existing work orders. Its only effect is state open → accepted for the selected existing record. It is available only when that record's stored state is open. After acceptance a repeated invocation must be disabled or a no-op; do not duplicate or delete a record, and do not change any other field. Preserve the table, search on title only, priority equality filter, captions, column order and original fixture values. This is a local prototype operation, with no external service.

Extend this existing prototype with a Teams directory. Team T-A has name "Mechanical" and active true. Team T-B has name "Electrical" and active false. Add team_id to the existing work orders: w1 has team_id T-A, w2 has team_id T-B, w3 has team_id T-A. Relate team_id to the team identity and show the related team name, not only its ID, in the work-order table and selected-record details. Keep the existing state/priority/title/hours columns in their existing relative order. Preserve all other source data, search, filter and Accept semantics.

Organize the same prototype into top-level tabs "Work orders" and "Teams". Work orders must retain its table, title-only search, priority filter, Accept command and selected-order read-only details including the related team name. Teams must have a table and selected-team read-only details. Selecting a work order must never change the selected team on the other tab; switching tabs must not lose either selection. Preserve all source records, relationships, captions and relative work-order column order. At width 390px all tabs, search, filters and actions must remain available without horizontal overflow.

On the existing Teams tab add a separate read-only work-order table titled "Orders for selected team". This is a second view of the existing work-order resource, not a new resource or copied records. On entry start with no team selected, intentionally replacing only the previous initial Team selection; once chosen retain each tab's independent selection across tab switches. With no team selected it shows all three work orders. Selecting team T-A filters only this secondary table to w1 and w3; selecting T-B filters it to w2. It must display the related team name and the work-order title, state, priority and hours. This team-driven filter must not affect the global Repair queue table on Work orders, its title-only search or its independent priority filter. Preserve all original source data and live edits, work-order details, captions/order and open-only Accept. Do not add any write operation or external service.

Add a read-only Checklists directory to the existing Work orders tab.
Record c1: work_id w1, description "Check seal", done false.
Record c2: work_id w1, description "Read pressure", done true.
Record c3: work_id w3, description "Check calibration", done false.
Relate work_id to the existing work-order identity. Show all three checklist records and all their source fields in a table, displaying the related work-order title rather than just its ID. Selecting a work order in the global Repair queue table must emphasize, not filter, its related checklist rows: w1 emphasizes c1 and c2; w2 emphasizes none; w3 emphasizes c3. All three checklist rows must remain visible in every case. This is intentionally different from the Teams tab's filtered Orders for selected team table; retain that filtering and keep the selection drivers independent. Preserve the two tabs, both directories, their details/relationships, every source fixture and live edit, existing search/filter, captions/order and open-only Accept. Do not add a write operation or external integration.

On the existing Work orders tab add a separate read-only chart of hours by work-order title, using the existing work-order resource. Show one point per existing work order, with its actual title and hours, not an aggregation or a computed replacement. Do not replace the global Repair queue table or copy records into a new resource. The chart always shows all three work orders even when global title search or the priority filter hides table rows; choosing a Team must still filter only Orders for selected team. Preserve both tabs, related names and details, source fixtures and live edits, existing captions and relative column order, title-only search, priority equality filtering, stored-open-only Accept, Team filtering and selection isolation, and the Checklists directory with work-order-driven emphasis rather than filtering. At 390px the chart and existing controls must remain reachable without page overflow. Add no write operation or external service.

On the existing Work orders tab add a separate read-only board of the existing work orders grouped by stored state. Each work order appears once as a card showing its title, priority and hours. Use the existing resource, not copied records or a new resource per state. Clicking a card selects that existing work order for the global Repair queue and the current Checklists emphasis; this global selection is deliberately shared, not a new independent selection. It must never change the selected Team or its secondary-table filter. Keep all board records present when the global table's search or priority filter hides rows. Do not enable dragging, moving cards, editing or a new write command. Preserve the global table and its captions/order, title-only search, priority filter, open-only Accept, both tabs, related names/details, source fixtures/live edits, independent Team selection/filtering, all Checklist rows with emphasis, and the independent hours chart. At 390px every state lane and card must be reachable without page overflow. No external service.

extension_policy: After the preceding logical level is functionally qualified at its declared effort, preregister each further supported ABI combination and independent oracle before inference. A prior low failure is retained when high advances; do not relabel that as an unbroken low staircase. Stop an actual ABI capacity/gap as such; do not call it a model reasoning boundary.
upper_bound_policy: First observed failure requires attribution and repeated frozen logical task. One failure alone is not a reliability threshold. A model-only exact-wire reasoning claim requires compare_reasoning_inputs eligibility, not normalization of changed plan IDs.
